title: Trace enumeration, deferred iterator execution and enumerator disposal on normal exit or failure

options: Calling `Values` creates the sequence; validation runs when `foreach` calls `MoveNext` outside the `try`.
Calling `Values` validates the input; enumeration later rethrows the exception stored during that call.
Calling `Values` schedules background execution; validation runs after control has left the `try`.
Calling `Values` runs validation immediately; iterator exceptions bypass catches surrounding the method call.

rubric.point: Selects the explanation that iterator-body validation executes during enumeration outside the surrounding try block.

questions.model: Calling `Values` creates the sequence; its body first runs when `foreach` calls `MoveNext`, outside the `try`.

rubric.point: Explains that foreach disposes this iterator's enumerator when the loop body throws, through its cleanup path.
Explains that disposing the suspended iterator executes its pending finally block, which prints released.

questions.model: When the loop body throws, `foreach` disposes the enumerator during exception unwinding. Disposal runs the iterator's pending `finally`, printing `released` before the exception propagates to the caller.

c2.text: IEnumerable materialized in foreach heade, when first move next is called, then the foreach body is executed

c1.feedback: The answer is “Calling `Values` creates the sequence; validation runs when `foreach` calls `MoveNext` outside the `try`.”.

annotations.quote: IEnumerable materialized in foreach heade, when first move next is called
annotations.note: You describe deferred execution starting at the first MoveNext, which is true but does not address why `released` prints when the body throws. The question asks about disposal, not when iteration begins.

annotations.quote: then the foreach body is executed
annotations.note: You needed to say that foreach disposes the enumerator when the body throws, and that disposing the suspended iterator runs its pending `finally`, printing `released`.

c2.feedback: You described deferred iteration start but never explained the disposal on exception or the pending `finally` running, so neither rubric point is earned.
